title: OpenHydroLab: interactive, physics-accurate animations for teaching hydraulics and hydrology
description:
OpenHydroLab is an open-source suite of eight interactive browser laboratories for teaching undergraduate hydraulics and hydrology. Every displayed quantity is computed live from the governing equation, and every module runs offline from a local file, with no installation and no third-party host. Seven modules are single self-contained HTML pages; the 3D channel-geometry laboratory is a page plus a vendored copy of Three.js under animations/vendor/three/, which must be kept alongside it.

Modules: channel geometry and the Froude number, Manning uniform flow, specific energy and choking, hydraulic jumps, gradually varied flow profiles, storm hydrographs, the unit hydrograph workbench, and an IDF/frequency-analysis pipeline on a real 27-year gauge record.

Release 1.0.2 adds the verification harness: 118 distinct numerical cases, executed across Chromium, Firefox and WebKit to yield 354 comparison records, together with 88 software, offline-delivery and accessibility checks repeated on the three engines (264 runs). Every reference value is derived independently of the code. The verification protocol is documented in validation/validation-protocol.md and the generated dataset in validation/results/. This protocol establishes computational fidelity and reproducibility only; it makes no claim about learning outcomes.
